WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
At Horeb the LORD told Elijah: “anoint Hazael to be king over Syria”. 1 Kings 19:15
“Him that escapeth the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay.” 1 Kings 19:17

Elisha wept and told him: “I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.” 2 Kings 8:11–12
Hazael answered: “is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing?” Elisha: “The LORD hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.” 2 Kings 8:13
“In those days the LORD began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel.” 2 Kings 10:32
The LORD “delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, all their days”. 2 Kings 13:3
“So Hazael king of Syria died; and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his stead.” 2 Kings 13:24
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
To buy him off, Jehoash of Judah gave up the hallowed things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah had dedicated, his own hallowed things, and the gold of the house of the LORD. 2 Kings 12:18
Tribute from Judah: Jehoash sent it all “to Hazael king of Syria: and he went away from Jerusalem”. 2 Kings 12:18
He took from Israel the land east of the Jordan: Gilead, Gad, Reuben and Manasseh, as far as the Arnon, Gilead and Bashan. 2 Kings 10:32–33
“Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.” 2 Kings 13:22
Jehoahaz “besought the LORD”, and “the LORD gave Israel a saviour, so that they went out from under the hand of the Syrians”. 2 Kings 13:4–5
Amos: “they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron”. Amos 1:3

DATES DIFFER

FROM SHALMANESER III'S RECORDS AND SCRIPTURE, ON THE MAIN SYSTEM'S DATES

Already king of Damascus in Shalmaneser III's eighteenth year (841 BC); in his fourteenth year (845 BC) the king of Damascus was still Hadad-ezer. His death is not dated by any record used here: Scripture puts it after he had oppressed Israel “all the days of Jehoahaz”, who died in 798 BC on Thiele, McFall and Young's dates.
Not literally: he was told he would be king
Keil holds that only Jehu was really anointed; “Hazael was merely told by Elisha that he would be king” (2 Kings 8:13), so the word is used figuratively here. 2 Kings 8:13 [22]
Anointed in secret by Elijah, then again by Elisha
Earlier interpreters, as reported (and rejected) by Keil (tr. 1872), p. 260

Keil reports the opinion that Elijah anointed Hazael and Jehu at once but kept it secret, and that Elisha repeated it when their time came; he finds it ruled out by the account of Jehu's anointing in 2 Kings 9.[22]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture records the command to anoint Hazael (1 Kings 19:15) but no anointing.
Scripture does not name Hazael's father; Shalmaneser's inscription calls him “the son of a nobody”.
Scripture gives him no length of reign and no burial.
Scripture says nothing of his wars with Assyria.
Chronicles tells of a Syrian army in Joash's day without naming Hazael (2 Chronicles 24:23–24).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textThe Hazael of 1 Kings 19 and 2 Kings 8–13. Amos's “house of Hazael” names his line. 1 Kings 19:15 Amos 1:4

Scholars' viewPublished summaries of the editors' reports say that A. Biran and J. Naveh (1995) credit the Aramaic stele from Tel Dan to Hazael, and that the king's name does not survive on the fragments found; the editors' articles themselves were not read for this page.[11]
